intro:
Use it to compare named things on three measures at once: growth, margin and revenue for a set of products. Each row of `data` is one circle. `xDataKey` and `yDataKey` place it, `sizeKey` sets its area and `labelKey` names it. Colour cycles by row, or comes from `colorKey`.

Area is hard to judge exactly, and overlapping circles hide each other, so it suits a dozen or two named rows. For many unnamed rows, use a [Scatter Chart](/docs/web/charts/scatter-chart).

parts.Header: The strip above the plot: `title`, `value` and `caption`, with your own control on the trailing side.
parts.Grid: Lines both ways, in the theme's border colour. `rows` and `columns` are roughly how many: the axes pick round numbers near them.
parts.Quadrants: A crosshair splitting the plot into four, with an optional word for each corner. It stands at the mean of each axis unless `x` and `y` pin it.
parts.Trend: The straight line that fits the cloud best, dashed and under the circles. `onFit` gives you the slope, the intercept and how tight the fit is.
parts.Bubbles: The circles. Without this part nothing is drawn or readable.
parts.Labels: The names, inside the circles. A bubble under `minRadius` goes without, and a name longer than its circle is cut.
parts.SizeKey: Three nested circles saying what an area is worth, over a corner of the plot. It needs `sizeKey` on the chart.
parts.Skeleton: A still field of muted circles, drawn only while `status` is `loading`.
parts.XAxis: Value labels under the plot, in round numbers. `label` names the axis.
parts.YAxis: Value labels down the side, in round numbers. `label` names the axis.
parts.Tooltip: Makes the field readable by pointer and keyboard, and floats a readout beside what is being read. `showLabel={false}` keeps the reading without the readout. `labels` names the keys in it.
parts.Legend: A swatch and a name per row, under the plot, up to `limit`.

examples.title: Quadrants
examples.description: `BubbleChart.Quadrants` splits the plot at the mean of each axis and names the corners. Pass `x` and `y` to split at a target instead. Set `tint={false}` when all four corners matter equally.

examples.title: Trend
examples.description: `BubbleChart.Trend` fits a straight line through the circles. `onFit` reports how tight the fit is, and fires only when the numbers change, so it can go straight into state.

examples.title: Size key
examples.description: Area has no axis to read it off, so `BubbleChart.SizeKey` shows what the smallest, middle and largest areas are worth. Place it in the corner the circles leave empty.

examples.title: Colours and a legend
examples.description: `colorKey` reads a colour from each row: a theme role, any CSS colour, or a number from 1 to 5 naming a chart colour. `BubbleChart.Legend` lists the rows under the plot.

examples.title: Loading, then data
examples.description: Add `BubbleChart.Skeleton` and drive `status`. The placeholder circles stay still, because a shimmer would read as them moving. The real bubbles grow in where they belong when it turns `ready`.

examples.title: Changing data
examples.description: When `data` changes, the circles, names, rules and axes move to their new values over `domainDuration`, and a bubble keeps its identity through its row. A `ref` on the chart has `replay()`, which grows the bubbles in again.

notes:
### Rows

A row with no finite number at `xDataKey` or `yDataKey` draws no bubble, and a numeric string does not count as a number. Convert strings before passing the data.

### Sizing

The chart fills its container's width and takes its height from `aspectRatio`, which applies to the plot alone, so a header does not shrink it. The default of `1` suits a bubble field.

Every edge of the plot holds back the largest radius in `sizeRange`, so raising it costs room. On a narrow screen, lower `sizeRange` before lowering anything else.

### Domains

Each axis is the data's extent widened to round numbers, and neither is floored at zero. `xDomain` and `yDomain` fix one instead, which also keeps the frame still when the data changes.

### Reading

A mouse reads the nearest bubble as it moves. A tap reads one, and a sideways drag reads the bubbles it passes. A click or a tap pins the reading until the next press elsewhere or Escape. The arrow keys walk the bubbles once the chart has focus. `onActivePointChange` gives you the bubble being read, for a readout outside the chart.

### Accessibility

The chart renders a list of its rows for screen readers, and `label` and `labelForDatum` set what it says. With reduced motion set, the bubbles appear at their final size without the entrance, and data changes jump to their new places. `animationDuration={0}` draws the bubbles at once for everybody.
propsNote: `BubbleChart`, `BubbleChart.Header`, `BubbleChart.SizeKey` and `BubbleChart.Legend` also take the props of the element they render, and a `className`. `BubbleChart.Tooltip` puts its `className` on the readout. The other parts draw nothing themselves and take only the props listed.
